title: Sum and filter
description: Given a list of integers, use a Stream to filter only those greater than 10 and sum them. Print the result of the sum.
hints: numeros.stream() creates the stream from the list
.filter(n -> n > 10) filters the elements that meet the condition
solutionExplanation: The stream filters numbers greater than 10 (12, 15, 20, 25, 11 = 83). mapToInt converts Integer to primitive int to use sum().

title: Process text
description: Given a list of Java code lines, use a Stream to filter the lines containing the word "Java" (regardless of uppercase/lowercase), convert them to uppercase and print each one. At the end print how many lines were found.
hints: .forEach(System.out::println) prints each element of the stream
.count() returns the number of elements that passed the filter
solutionExplanation: filter with a lambda checks if the line contains "java" (case insensitive). peek allows executing an action (printing in uppercase) without altering the stream. count() returns the final count.

title: Group and reduce
description: Given a list of people (name, age, city), use Streams to: 1) Group by city using Collectors.groupingBy, 2) For each group, calculate the average age, 3) Print each city with its average age.
hints: Collectors.groupingBy(Persona::ciudad) groups by city in a Map<String, List<Persona>>
Use .ifPresentOrElse() or .orElse(0.0) to handle the OptionalDouble
solutionExplanation: Collectors.groupingBy groups the people by city. Collectors.averagingInt calculates the average age automatically for each group. The result is a Map<String, Double> that is printed with forEach.
